commands.review_summary:
This PR updates Claude bundle-MCP argument handling to collect and merge all variadic `--mcp-config` values and adds a regression test for multiple config files.

PR surface: Source +34, Tests +49. Total +83 across 3 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection on current `main` shows `--mcp-config a.json b.json` consumes only `a.json`, leaves `b.json` in argv, and merges only the first file.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] A narrow automated repair can fix the optional-args type error while preserving the intended variadic parser behavior.

target.title: fix: collect all variadic --mcp-config values instead of only the first (fixes #98944)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`injectClaudeMcpConfigArgs` (`src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp-claude.ts:26-47`) treats `--mcp-config` as taking exactly one value, but the repo's own Claude arg model treats it as variadic: `extensions/anthropic/cli-shared.ts:253-260` puts it in `CLAUDE_SIDE_QUESTION_VARIADIC_VALUE_ARGS` and skips all following non-dash values (`:290-297`). `findClaudeMcpConfigPath` (`bundle-mcp-claude.ts:9-23`) likewise returns only the first value, so only the first user config file is merged (`bundle-mcp.ts:191-208`).

A user configuring `cliBackends["claude-cli"].args: [..., "--mcp-config", "a.json", "b.json"]` gets: `--mcp-config a.json` stripped, `b.json` left behind as a bare positional (which Claude `-p` treats as the prompt or errors on), and `b.json`'s servers silently dropped from the merged strict config. Valid config produces a broken run.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix aligns `--mcp-config` handling in the bundler with the variadic arg model already used by the anthropic extension's `stripClaudeSideQuestionConflictingArgs`. Three changes in two files:

1. **`findAllClaudeMcpConfigPaths`** (new helper in `bundle-mcp-claude.ts`): collects all `--mcp-config` values using the same variadic skip pattern — every non-dash token after `--mcp-config` until the next flag is a separate config file path.
2. **`injectClaudeMcpConfigArgs`** (`bundle-mcp-claude.ts`): updated to skip all following non-flag values after `--mcp-config` instead of only one.
3. **`prepareCliBundleMcpConfig`** (`bundle-mcp.ts`): reads and merges all user config files into the bundle overlay, not just the first.

The existing `findClaudeMcpConfigPath` signature is preserved (delegates to `findAllClaudeMcpConfigPaths(args)[0]`) so callers that only need the first path are unaffected.

## User Impact

Users who pass multiple `--mcp-config` files to the Claude CLI backend will now have all their MCP servers correctly merged into the bundle overlay config, instead of only the first file being read and subsequent files leaking as bare positional args.

## Evidence

- [x] AI-assisted (Hermes Agent)
- **Behavior addressed:** The CLI runner bundler only reads the first `--mcp-config` file when multiple are provided, leaving subsequent file paths as bare positional arguments and silently dropping their MCP servers from the merged config.
- **Environment tested:** macOS 26.4.1, Node 22.22.3, OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (2913d3a)
- **Steps run after the patch:** Ran the bundle-mcp verification suite which exercises `prepareCliBundleMcpConfig` with `args: ["./fake-claude.mjs", "--mcp-config", "a.json", "b.json"]` against two real config files containing distinct MCP servers.
- **Evidence after fix:** All 7 verification cases pass including the new variadic case. The merged overlay config contains both `serverA` (from `a.json`) and `serverB` (from `b.json`). Neither `a.json` nor `b.json` appears as a bare positional in the output args.
- **Observed result after fix:** Both user config files are read and merged into the bundle overlay. The `--mcp-config` flag correctly strips all variadic values.
- **What was not tested:** Live Claude CLI invocation with multiple `--mcp-config` files (requires claude-cli binary not available in this environment). The verification exercises the same production code path (`prepareCliBundleMcpConfig` → `findAllClaudeMcpConfigPaths` → `readExternalMcpConfig` → `applyMergePatch`).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The CLI runner bundler only reads the first `--mcp-config` file when multiple are provided, leaving subsequent file paths as bare positional arguments and silently dropping their MCP servers from the merged config.
- **Environment tested:** macOS 26.4.1, Node 22.22.3, OpenClaw 2026.6.11 (2913d3a)
- **Steps run after the patch:** Ran the bundle-mcp verification suite which exercises `prepareCliBundleMcpConfig` with `args: ["./fake-claude.mjs", "--mcp-config", "a.json", "b.json"]` against two real config files containing distinct MCP servers.
- **Evidence after fix:** All 7 verification cases pass including the new variadic case. The merged overlay config contains both `serverA` (from `a.json`) and `serverB` (from `b.json`). Neither `a.json` nor `b.json` appears as a bare positional in the output args.
- **Observed result after fix:** Both user config files are read and merged into the bundle overlay. The `--mcp-config` flag correctly strips all variadic values.
- **What was not tested:** Live Claude CLI invocation with multiple `--mcp-config` files (requires claude-cli binary not available in this environment). The verification exercises the same production code path (`prepareCliBundleMcpConfig` → `findAllClaudeMcpConfigPaths` → `readExternalMcpConfig` → `applyMergePatch`).
